about: Where Jerry's music goes (CL-21, CL-23, CL-24, CL-25, D-21; docs/audio/cue-sheet.md). Names are relative to assets/soundtrack/, without .mp3. A pool listed here replaces the default pool in core/audio.js. waveByDay: the track each wave loops, by day (Jerry: days 1-2 day skirmish B, 3-7 A, 8-11 Tier 1, 12-15 Tier 2, 16+ Tier 3; special nights use their day's track until they get their own). fight: the fallback. dayFight: daylight fights pick a track by horde size; sizes[i] is the smallest horde that gets tracks[i]. hits: seconds into a track where it hits (fights start and loop there). stings: cues. gain: loudness multiplier per track (Jerry's are boosted). The aftermath track is out for now (Jerry). The WAV originals stay in incoming/ and are not committed. CL-34 (Jerry): the fight beds are now chiptune loops made by tools/chip.py from the tempo and key of Jerry's Suno fight tracks (chip_*); they loop from 0, natively. The Suno fight files stay on disk until Jerry has heard the loops; the old compose.py metal bed is out of the ember pool. CL-35/36: day 1 has its own song, fight_day01 ('First Blood', tools/day1.py, 4:30 loop, gain 1.6, fades in over 1.5 s because its intro is the build); the stingers and cues are chiptune (tools/stingers.py) at gain 2.0. fadeIn: per-track fight fade-in seconds (default 10). Claude keeps this file. CL-42/43/47 (Jerry: day 1's music as good as possible): the day-1 song is also cut into sections (tools/day1.py -> fight_day01_sections.ogg, Opus) that the section player in core/audio.js moves between as the wave goes (sections.flow: stalk while the horde is out of sight, the fight rotation once one is within 'near' metres, the break after 'lullAfter' seconds with nobody within 'far', the climax for the last 'lastAt'); fight_day01.mp3 is the whole song, the fallback. The alarm is also the nightfall (2 bars, 5.0 s to the hit) and the relief sting is also the dawn (7.5 s, the finisher's length); 'dawn' is the dawn card's chime. The menu and the prep pools are chip tracks in the song's voices (tools/calm.py). CL-52: the day track (calm_day) is a 5-minute ambient circle played through Web Audio (a one-section 'sections' entry) so it loops without a seam; it is the only daytime track. 'camp' is the 2 s camp-cleared stinger, played while the day fight fades. CL-38: nights 2-20 have their own section songs in First Blood's family (tools/hordes.py): faster, in new keys and driving harder as the run climbs, with their own songs for the Ember and Guardian nights; waveByDay follows GB-53's table. After night 20 the finale keeps playing. CL-71 (P-21): nights 16 and 18 have their own late tiers, fight_ember_late (118 bpm, F minor, DRIVE 3) and fight_guardian_late (100 bpm, C minor, DRIVE 3), so they no longer reuse nights 4 and 6's songs. specials: a special night's own song, played instead of its day's when the page says it is that night (CL-77: fog -> fight_fognight, tools/fog.py). fight_heart: the guardian's last fight in the heart (CL-85, tools/heart.py), played by its phase (flow.phases) rather than the wave's. CL-128 (Jerry's playthrough 1: 'Better Music deserving special attention each night'; his reference a chiptune mix, and he likes 'everything' in it): every night 2-20 has its own song (tools/nights.py): its own hook, riff, bridge, chords, key, mode, tempo, groove, bass and lead, from 108 bpm on night 2 to 152 on night 20, which comes home to First Blood's key and sings its hook in the climax. Night 14 is Fog Night and plays fight_fognight (specials); its waveByDay entry is night 13's song, the fallback while the fog song decodes. The old First Blood family (fight_n02 ... fight_guardian_late, tools/hordes.py) is out of waveByDay and sections; its files stay on disk until Jerry has heard the new ones. CL-165 (Jerry: 'wire them in. Lets see how they do. Definitely keep our old stuff as backup'): this is the ElevenLabs set. Nights 1-20 play Jerry's ElevenLabs songs (elevenlabs/night-NN), cut into the same seven sections on their own bar grid; a climax that rings out loops only its full bars. Night 14 (fog) plays night-14. The heart plays elevenlabs/heart_sections.ogg under the fight_heart name. Day fights play elevenlabs/day-horde-1..5, a bar-aligned loop cut out of each take (no intro or ending), looping natively from 0 like the chip loops did. Gains match the old songs' loudness. The old set is music-old.json and every old file is still here; 'Switch music (old - new).bat' at the game's root swaps them. CL-167 (Jerry: 'We are keeping the new night songs, but we are going to use your original day fight songs'): dayFight is the chip loops again (chip_skirmish_b, chip_skirmish_a, chip_fight_1..3, as in music-old.json). The ElevenLabs day-horde loops stay in elevenlabs/ and keep their gains here, unused. CL-265 (Jerry's N31: 'The metal stinger for the alarm that he used to have is missing'; revises D-33): the alarm plays his Suno metal sting again (sting_alarm_metal, from incoming/sting_alarm.wav, brought to the stings' loudness), on top of the klaxon; the fight comes in when it ends. The chiptune sting_alarm stays on disk.

score.about: CL-275 (D-97): the 1.2 score from F:\Music. Each night a suite of Hellshot kits, three layers each (gh/*.ogg, git-ignored: made on Jerry's PC by tools/music-make.py). Opt-in until it covers every moment: ?score=1 or localStorage tt_score=1. A night's gain matches the loudness of the song it replaces; fallback is that song (played when the gh files are not on this machine).
